rawContent: This cultural moment shouldn't be about thinking all is unforgivable or turning backs on friends, but making clear once and for all what respecting people means and what #consent means. #metoo #timesup re: @JRKaiman @laura__tucker allegations. https://t.co/v5HsiuG4bb

@StephenMcDonell @JRKaiman Stephen, do you condone the alleged behaviour that Laura T. outlined in her post? If true, she absolutely has a genuine grievance.  As a rape victim, I do not feel at all belittled by Laura's decision to tell her story.  Don't speculate on intentions of women who started #metoo

Spent the day talking with Chinese students about #metoo and they were overwhelmingly supportive of the movement and said authorities should treat the stories seriously. Spoke with two male students who organize self-defense courses for classmates. https://t.co/BOs7OZAgWq

Weibo trending topics #Metoo and  #me too反性侵运动# "anti-sexual assault campaign" still operating.  #MeToo在中国 (Me too in China) topic is deleted but I was still able to search for posts containing the hashtag. https://t.co/HPpFRw2oEK

Lawyer Guo Jianmei has been working on women's rights cases for 30 years. She says the social media powered #metoo #woyeshi anti-sexual assault campaign is the biggest women's rights movement she's seen in China. https://t.co/mFnkvTaRUL
Chinese https://t.co/rCXkmxJpYG story about professors signing anti-sexual harassment #metoo manifesto deleted, redirected to homepage: https://t.co/IRP6rC5faq
China's #Metoo emerges, testing censors' limits. My piece @AFP interviews women leading a social media powered movement in a country where any collective action is risky: https://t.co/jtoHHk0mBh

Why is #metoo political? "It is well documented that many Chinese officials treat women like playthings to use for pleasure. 

"The whole fabric of Chinese society disadvantages women. It's nearly impossible to sue about sexual harassment." - Guo Jianmei https://t.co/jtoHHk0mBh

But while #metoo was slow to catch on in China, in the past weeks it's exploded and helped raise public awareness when many people had "no concept of sexual harassment" before. My piece: https://t.co/jtoHHk0mBh

In the past week, censors deleted 100s of posts tagged "#Metoo in China" and closed forums. "Determined users can still have discussions in new channels. That is what I call 'soft censorship'," says @CDT @underbreath https://t.co/X93cZaVAFp #woyeshi
Authorities attempt to ban China's #metoo social media movement. I summarized my reporting on the issue on @RadioNational along with Dr. Zhiqiong Wang. Listen here: https://t.co/S9xU97iIcw

Free speech advocates worry that as increasingly complex wordplay is used in China to circumvent censorship, less people are able to engage. But the "#RiceBunny" (#MiTu) stand-in for #MeToo is both easy to understand and funny, possibly drawing even more attention to the issues. https://t.co/aDTnpNi455
Rice Bunny (#MiTu instead of #MeToo) is also a funny anti-censorship move from Chinese feminists because Wechat's most popular animated stickers are bunny-themed. https://t.co/Yg2CB4cQGW
For context on why #MeToo is partially censored in China, see my piece: https://t.co/jtoHHk0mBh https://t.co/pNHkyMpzZg

Excited to kick off the @BeijingBookworm Literary Festival moderating a panel on #MeToo and other major issues in women's lives in China for the past year. Panelists: @LenoraChu, @women_podcast, Dan Bao. Will be in English and Mandarin March 8 #WomensDay: https://t.co/OZCOwKliFo
We have a Twitter. Shit getting real! https://t.co/uMwXEiZlNB #WomensDay #womenshistorymonth #womensday2018 #MeToo #TimesUp #GenderPayGap #genderchat

Sophia Huang, a prominent journalist in China's #MeToo movement, reposted a letter criticizing the constitution change to her WeChat account, adding her own take.

Later that day, her account was shut down. She wasn't impressed, and spoke with me about it: https://t.co/2ykEQtzQiJ https://t.co/73jnrmboRT
Survey: More than 80% of female journalists harassed in workplace. https://t.co/Hx35vvpVb3 #metoo #womensday

Follow our discussion on #metoo #mettooinchina happening now at the @BeijingBookworm literary festival. Hashtag: #Nuvoices. Yajun of @women_podcast: "I was surprised at how Me Too exploded in #China The impact can't be understated." #womensday #WomensDay2018 https://t.co/JzORi2IjAD

It took years for people in America to go from "no means no" to "yes means yes". In China we are still dealing with the "No means yes" movement - writer Dan Bao on #metoo #mettooinchina #Nuvoices #womensday https://t.co/6cKASpX6UO

Why didn't she want to be an architect? She had the education. She didn't feel like she had the #power. "I don't see women wanting to take back their power here and that worries me." #metoo #mettooinchina #womensday #Nuvoices @BeijingBookworm Literary Festival. @LenoraChu https://t.co/eVhL5O5oQJ

Who's missing in discussions about #metoo #mettooinchina? Many lower class women, women who didn't grow up in big cities. My ayi (housekeeper) had three kids by 29 and had no choice about it. - @women_podcast #Nuvoices https://t.co/ePU2zbYXl2

I think sexual harassment, especially in #China, is more about power than sex. Men who are harassing women dominate positions of power. - @LenoraChu #womensday #mettooinchina #metoo #Nuvoices https://t.co/FHuWXDuXgJ

The #genderpaygap is actually worse in China than it was decades ago. Women make 67% of what men make in same jobs. @LenoraChu #womensday #mettooinchina #metoo #Nuvoices #paygap https://t.co/zGkTa1U2AO

Report also includes a new case study on how #MeToo took off in China, after women connected with each other on social media and worked together to spread Luo Qianqian's story and defend against her attackers. Pg. 48: https://t.co/iZHd7sLzmt https://t.co/zlVVn71IsI

The @n3conference agenda seems so interesting this year, with some of the most talented Asian women in journalism including @AngieTVLau @stegersaurus @laurelchor @trinnaleong @YvonneLeow. Looking forward to chatting about foreign correspondence and #metoo https://t.co/p3lKEExnX7

What Is the Significance of China’s #MeToo Movement? Great conversation here with contributions from Chinese feminist activists and researchers with first-hand observations: https://t.co/gOCNBkIbjc via @chinafile

Looks mild but have to remember that organized action among students at top Chinese universities is rare because of the possible consequences. Students who signed petitions in support of  #metoo have gotten interrogated by school officials. https://t.co/h5eiifYPdJ
ICYMI fascinating story by AFP's new China correspondent @poori_w: #MeToo activists use blockchain to skirt China censors https://t.co/ZgPfIVjdF2

Renee Ren said her lawsuit was inspired by "photos of women's marches around the world".

In what is thought to be the first case of its kind, Ren is suing police over their "inaction" and she's doing it on her own without legal rep. My story:  https://t.co/xuDja8wc0p #MeToo

In a 2017 survey of Chinese students, 70% reported having been sexually harassed. Over 40% said the cases took place on campus.

But only 4% of women and even fewer men reported campus cases to police. My report on one student who is fighting back:

https://t.co/qsvXh4q20t #MeToo

With police refusing to investigate, she gave up -- until the #MeToo movement ignited in China.

It was this public outpouring that prompted Ren to file her lawsuit -- despite pressure from her university to drop the case.

"They called my parents." 

https://t.co/qsvXh4q20t
Second allegation of sexual misconduct against LA Times Beijing Bureau Chief Jon Kaiman surfaces https://t.co/E5OnzDXBQv #metoo

"Somewhere deep in the Chinese surveillance apparatus there is a startling collection of images of journalists’ genitalia." So. I just unleashed this onto the world, with editor @BeijingPalmer https://t.co/9xCqo8s30R #metoo

The #MeToo campaign has reminded us of how common stories like mine are — but the behavior of foreign men working abroad has been far worse than anything I ever experienced at home. The phenomenon is especially problematic for journalists. Please read: https://t.co/9xCqo8s30R

Thanks all for reading! @BeijingPalmer and I spent months on this and I'm so excited people have reacted immediately so positively. It's like Christmas morning x 100! #metoo #fuckyeah! https://t.co/ddQ1emgdnu

I've had male friends write to say how they're so sorry that these things happened to me. But women know how common they are, especially in Asia for the reasons listed in the piece. #metoo https://t.co/QSmGCB8y25

.@AP news director for Koreas and Japan Ken Moritsugu on benefits of diverse newsroom: For example as a man, he might not have recognized the start of #metoo movement for weeks. https://t.co/NDtDBH9WXk

Panel takeaways on covering #MeToo: maintain rigorous reporting and corroborate facts as much as possible, anticipate negative reactions and prepare, explain structural power imbalances, be aware of toll of reporting on trauma and make time for self care. #N3Con2018 https://t.co/MDV7WiKdDH

Attention! @nvvoices needs your help to help sexual assault survivors. Please consider providing suggestions of resources (hotlines, shelters, etc) and we'll organize into an accessible document in different languages. #MeToo #TimesUp https://t.co/7tqRJe53sC

Webinars are totally nerdy, but I hope this session I did on "Managing #MeToo in Newsrooms" for @NewspaperWorld is a helpful resource for managers and journalists interested in shaping newsroom policy and preventing #sexualharassment and assault cases. https://t.co/9jcwASP4SU

This webinar was based on my reporting, consultations with journalists and legal professionals and this great new handbook from WAN-IFRA @NewspaperWorld. My personal research on  this topic is a work in progress. https://t.co/6EZvp7oc6B #MeToo

This webinar was based on my reporting, consultations with journalists and legal professionals and this great new handbook from WAN-IFRA @NewspaperWorld. My personal research on this topic is a work in progress. Your feedback much appreciated! #MeToo https://t.co/9jcwASP4SU

"If people don't know there is a sexual harassment policy, it's not an effective policy." How can newsrooms ensure that employees know exactly what constitutes "sexual misconduct" and prevent harassment and abuse? My workshop on #MeToo in Media: https://t.co/h3DlMuGKQU

"Managers can underestimate how nervous people can be about bringing forth cases. For example, as a young woman you may not want your first interaction with a top manager to be about something you find embarrassing." My workshop: https://t.co/h3DlMuGKQU @NewspaperWorld #MeToo

I got to combine my passions, sex ed and journalism, as well as combating sexual harassment, in this free online workshop for @NewspaperWorld. Watch here or bookmark for later, and do send to newsroom managers! We can all play a role. https://t.co/h3DlMuGKQU #MeToo https://t.co/bROcuTGLCb
